02 · Differential expression

Load packages

pacman::p_load(here, limpa, limma, dplyr, ggplot2, purrr, tibble, tidyr, writexl)
here::i_am("02_Differential_Expression/02_Differential/a_script/02_differential.qmd")
here() starts at /Users/dtl0018/Desktop/A_Proteomics_Analysis/2026/BFR/BFR_limpa

Read proteins and design

proteins holds the normalised log2 abundances and their standard errors; d holds the design, the contrasts and the baseline contrast’s name. Design rows and matrix columns must name the same samples in the same order; equal dimensions alone would not catch a swapped sample.

proteins <- readRDS(here("01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "proteins.rds"))
d <- readRDS(here("02_Differential_Expression", "01_Design", "c_data", "design.rds"))
fitted_slope_file <- here(
  "01_Preprocess", "02_Quantification", "c_data", "quant_runs", "proteins_slope_fitted.rds"
)

stopifnot(identical(rownames(d$design), colnames(proteins$E)))

Fit

limpa’s sequence is dpcDE(), contrasts.fit(), eBayes(), topTable(). dpcDE() takes the place of lmFit() because only it reads the standard errors from dpcQuant(), as precision weights. sample.weights = TRUE adds one quality weight per sample, since removing contaminant rows does not undo what a bloody biopsy did to the rest of the sample; the weights are saved before contrasts.fit(), which drops them. contrasts.fit() forms the five comparisons and eBayes() moderates each protein’s variance toward a prior fitted across all proteins; robust = TRUE keeps proteins with outlying variances from distorting that prior.

fit <- dpcDE(proteins, d$design, sample.weights = TRUE)
First sample weights (min/max) 0.0881122/3.6280600
Final sample weights (min/max) 0.08897381/3.62043513
sample_weights <- fit$targets$sample.weight
fit <- contrasts.fit(fit, d$contrasts)
fit <- eBayes(fit, robust = TRUE)

A lower weight reduces a sample’s contribution without dropping it. Weights that differ between groups deserve a look but do not by themselves invalidate the model.

tibble(group = proteins$targets$group, weight = sample_weights) |>
  summarise(
    n = n(), median_weight = round(median(weight), 2),
    lowest_weight = round(min(weight), 2), .by = group
  )
# A tibble: 4 × 4
  group       n median_weight lowest_weight
  <chr>   <int>         <dbl>         <dbl>
1 HLRT_T1    33          1.05          0.16
2 HLRT_T2    33          1.12          0.28
3 BFR_T1     33          1.17          0.09
4 BFR_T2     32          0.98          0.29

From the fitted standard errors, the interaction effect each protein would need for 80% power at an unadjusted two-sided 0.05 threshold, on the log2 scale: median and 90th percentile across proteins. It describes sensitivity; it is not an FDR-adjusted power analysis or evidence of equivalence.

se <- fit$stdev.unscaled[, "Modality_x_Time_Interaction"] * sqrt(fit$s2.post)
round(quantile(se * (qt(0.975, fit$df.total) + qt(0.80, fit$df.total)), c(0.5, 0.9)), 3)
  50%   90% 
0.521 0.916

Results

topTable() takes the fit and one contrast and returns one row per protein. sort.by = "none" keeps protein order (the default sorts on the B statistic). Benjamini–Hochberg (BH) adjustment controls the false discovery rate within each contrast, not across all five.

results <- map(colnames(d$contrasts), function(cn) {
  topTable(fit, coef = cn, number = Inf, sort.by = "none") |>
    rownames_to_column("protein") |>
    mutate(contrast = cn, .before = 1)
}) |>
  list_rbind()

contrast_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    n_tested = n(),
    n_fdr_05 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.05),
    n_fdr_10 = sum(adj.P.Val < 0.10),
    min_adj_p = min(adj.P.Val),
    .by = contrast
  )
contrast_summary |>
  mutate(min_adj_p = signif(min_adj_p, 3))
                     contrast n_tested n_fdr_05 n_fdr_10 min_adj_p
1                BFR_Post-Pre     3042       60      132  2.62e-05
2               HLRT_Post-Pre     3042      107      177  2.18e-08
3            BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre     3042        0        0  9.99e-01
4          BFR_Post-HLRT_Post     3042        0        0  1.00e+00
5 Modality_x_Time_Interaction     3042        0        0  1.00e+00

Inspect p-value distributions

Per contrast: the estimated share of true nulls (propTrueNull()), the median absolute t and the fraction of p below 0.2. They describe the distributions; they do not prove calibration or explain an absence of discoveries.

null_summary <- results |>
  summarise(
    prop_true_null = round(propTrueNull(P.Value), 3),
    median_abs_t = round(median(abs(t)), 3),
    p_below_0.2 = round(mean(P.Value < 0.2), 3), .by = contrast
  )
null_summary
                     contrast prop_true_null median_abs_t p_below_0.2
1                BFR_Post-Pre          0.797        0.933       0.342
2               HLRT_Post-Pre          0.810        0.921       0.346
3            BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre          1.000        0.554       0.109
4          BFR_Post-HLRT_Post          1.000        0.592       0.147
5 Modality_x_Time_Interaction          1.000        0.519       0.100

The dashed line is the count per bin if p-values were uniform.

ggplot(results, aes(P.Value)) +
  geom_histogram(binwidth = 0.05, boundary = 0, fill = "grey35") +
  geom_hline(yintercept = nrow(proteins) / 20, linetype = 2, colour = "firebrick") +
  facet_wrap(~contrast) +
  labs(x = "p", y = "proteins", caption = "dashed line marks a flat null") +
  theme_minimal()

Significant and large enough

treat() tests whether |logFC| exceeds a threshold, here log2(1.15), a 15% change, rather than filtering significant results on fold change afterwards, which controls no error rate. The threshold is a study choice fixed in advance, not swept; its rationale is not yet documented.

ft <- treat(fit, lfc = log2(1.15), robust = TRUE)
treat_summary <- enframe(colSums(decideTests(ft) != 0), "contrast", "n_q_05")
treat_summary
# A tibble: 5 × 2
  contrast                    n_q_05
  <chr>                        <dbl>
1 BFR_Post-Pre                     0
2 HLRT_Post-Pre                    9
3 BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre                 0
4 BFR_Post-HLRT_Post               0
5 Modality_x_Time_Interaction      0

The pi score

The pi score, P.Value^abs(logFC), ranks the two within-leg contrasts so that large effects with small p come first. It controls no error rate and selects nothing. The mean number of observed precursors per sample sits beside it, because the top of a pi ranking is often thinly observed.

obs_per_sample <- rowMeans(proteins$other$n.observations)

results |>
  filter(contrast %in% c("BFR_Post-Pre", "HLRT_Post-Pre")) |>
  mutate(pi_score = P.Value^abs(logFC)) |>
  slice_min(pi_score, n = 10, by = contrast) |>
  mutate(mean_obs = round(obs_per_sample[protein], 2)) |>
  select(contrast, protein, Genes, logFC, adj.P.Val, pi_score, NPrec, mean_obs)

Baseline comparison

The two legs before training. A difference here can be biological or technical; it is not automatically an upstream error. The row check guards against a contrast name that matches nothing, since sum(logical(0)) is zero and would look like an empty baseline.

baseline <- filter(results, contrast == d$baseline)
stopifnot(nrow(baseline) == nrow(proteins))
sum(baseline$adj.P.Val < 0.05)
[1] 0
slice_min(baseline, P.Value, n = 5) |>
  select(protein, Genes, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val)
  protein     Genes      logFC     P.Value adj.P.Val
1  Q0D2K2    KLHL30 -0.3457262 0.001381562 0.9994333
2  O75367 MACROH2A1 -1.2275936 0.004051857 0.9994333
3  Q96G03      PGM2 -0.5218516 0.004182038 0.9994333
4  Q8NFV4    ABHD11  0.4573450 0.006592490 0.9994333
5  Q6NW29     RWDD4  0.5573468 0.007179796 0.9994333

The count is printed, not asserted, so a difference lands in the report instead of halting it.

Slope sensitivity

When the fitted-slope checkpoint exists, it gets the same detection filter, normalisation and design, then the discovery counts are compared with the primary run. The checks confirm sample order and protein coverage; they cannot confirm the checkpoint came from the same precursors.

fitted_slope <- readRDS(fitted_slope_file)
fitted_slope <- fitted_slope[
  filterByDetection(fitted_slope, n.samples = min(table(fitted_slope$targets$group))),
]
fitted_slope$E <- normalizeBetweenArrays(fitted_slope$E, method = "cyclicloess")
stopifnot(identical(colnames(fitted_slope$E), rownames(d$design)))
refit <- dpcDE(fitted_slope, d$design, sample.weights = TRUE) |>
  contrasts.fit(d$contrasts) |>
  eBayes(robust = TRUE)
First sample weights (min/max) 0.08648871/3.72207269
Final sample weights (min/max) 0.08937383/3.71283939
primary_hits <- decideTests(fit) != 0
stopifnot(all(rownames(primary_hits) %in% rownames(refit)))
refit_hits <- decideTests(refit)[rownames(primary_hits), , drop = FALSE] != 0
rbind(
  slope_0.7 = colSums(primary_hits),
  fitted_curve = colSums(refit_hits),
  both = colSums(primary_hits & refit_hits)
)
             BFR_Post-Pre HLRT_Post-Pre BFR_Pre-HLRT_Pre BFR_Post-HLRT_Post

Save results

fit.rds keeps the fitted model for the stages that rebuild contrasts. 02_differential.xlsx holds DEP_matrix (one row per protein: log2 fold change, p and BH-adjusted p per contrast), discovery counts, sample weights and the distribution summaries.

dep_matrix <- results |>
  select(protein, Genes, NPrec, contrast, logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = contrast,
    values_from = c(logFC, P.Value, adj.P.Val),
    names_glue = "{contrast}_{.value}"
  )

out <- here("02_Differential_Expression", "02_Differential", "c_data")
saveRDS(fit, file.path(out, "fit.rds"))
sheets <- list(
  DEP_matrix = dep_matrix,
  contrast_summary = contrast_summary,
  sample_weights = data.frame(
    sample_id = colnames(proteins$E), group = proteins$targets$group, weight = sample_weights
  ),
  null_summary = null_summary,
  treat_summary = treat_summary
)
overview <- data.frame(
  sheet = names(sheets), rows = map_int(sheets, nrow), columns = map_int(sheets, ncol),
  description = c(
    "logFC, p and BH p per contrast",
    "Discoveries per contrast at FDR 0.05 and 0.10",
    "Sample identifiers, groups and quality weights",
    "Descriptive p-value and t-statistic summaries",
    "Discoveries against the 15 percent fold-change threshold"
  )
)
write_xlsx(c(list(overview = overview), sheets), file.path(out, "02_differential.xlsx"))
